title: The bass player nicknamed E-String; Chester Zardis ruled out
summary: Robertson explains that the bass violinist E-String got his name from always playing on the E string; Russell asks if it was Chester Zardis, and Robertson says no.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: How'd he get that name, E-String?
We used to call him E-String because when he first started to learn how to play, he loved to play all the time on the E-String. He was like Eastring. We could call it Eastring.
It wasn't Chester Zardis, wasn't it Chester?
No, no. You talking about Chester Jones?
The little fella, he used to jump up and down when he played.

No, it wasn't Chester. I know this other day. Chester. No, it wasn't him. No, this fella here. He belonged in Manderville too. Well, we had a fella. We had a fella out of that in there called Black Eagle. Black Eagle. He was playing trumpet too over there with us. Black Eagle. Yeah. Any time a man played his way out of penitentiary, you know he could play.
